functions.summary: The HalAllocateHardwareCounters function allocates a set of hardware performance counter resources.

functions.name: HalExamineMBR

functions.name: HalGetBusDataByOffset
functions.summary: >[!WARNING] >HalGetBusDataByOffset and HalSetBusDataByOffset are provided for backward compatibility but should be used only if the methods recommended in Accessing Device Configuration Space cannot be used.
functions.signature: ULONG HalGetBusDataByOffset(BUS_DATA_TYPE BusDataType, ULONG BusNumber, ULONG SlotNumber, PVOID Buffer, ULONG Offset, ULONG Length);

params.name: BusDataType
params.description: Bus data to retrieve. The upper bound on the bus types supported is always MaximumBusDataType. The only supported BusDataType is `PCIConfiguration` All other types are deprecated.

params.name: BusNumber
params.description: Zero-based and system-assigned number of the bus in systems with several buses of the same BusDataType. This argument also carries the segment number. To specify the segment number, use (Segment << 8) | BusNumber

params.name: SlotNumber
params.description: Logical slot number or location of the device. If you specify PCIConfiguration as the BusDataType, this value is a PCI_SLOT_NUMBER value, which is the slot and function numbers combined.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: Pointer to a caller-supplied buffer for configuration information specific to BusDataType.

params.name: Offset
params.description: Byte offset in the PCI_COMMON_CONFIG structure for which the requested information should be returned. Callers can use the system-defined constant PCI_COMMON_HDR_LENGTH to specify the device-specific area of PCI_COMMON_CONFIG.

params.name: Length
params.description: Maximum number of bytes in the Buffer.

returns.description: The return value is the actual length read from the config space.

functions.name: HalSetBusDataByOffset
functions.summary: >[!WARNING] >HalGetBusDataByOffset and HalSetBusDataByOffset are provided for backward compatibility but should be used only if the methods recommended in Accessing Device Configuration Space cannot be used.
functions.signature: ULONG HalSetBusDataByOffset(BUS_DATA_TYPE BusDataType, ULONG BusNumber, ULONG SlotNumber, PVOID Buffer, ULONG Offset, ULONG Length);

params.name: BusDataType
params.description: Bus data to set. This value can be PCIConfiguration. The upper bound on the types supported is always MaximumBusDataType.

params.name: BusNumber
params.description: Zero-based and system-assigned number of the bus in systems with several buses of the same BusDataType. This argument also carries the segment number. To specify the segment number, use (Segment << 8) | BusNumber

params.name: SlotNumber
params.description: Logical slot number or location of the device. If you specify PCIConfiguration as the BusDataType, this value is specified as a PCI_SLOT_NUMBER value, which is the slot and function numbers combined.

params.name: Buffer
params.description: Pointer to a caller-supplied buffer for configuration information specific to BusDataType.

params.name: Offset
params.description: Byte offset in the PCI_COMMON_CONFIG structure where the caller-supplied configuration values begin. Callers can use the system-defined constant PCI_COMMON_HDR_LENGTH to specify the device-specific area of PCI_COMMON_CONFIG.

params.name: Length
params.description: Number of bytes in Buffer.

returns.description: The return value is the actual length written to the config space.

functions.name: IoCreateFileEx
functions.summary: The IoCreateFileEx function either causes a new file or directory to be created, or opens an existing file, device, directory, or volume and gives the caller a handle for the file object. File system filter drivers (legacy filter drivers) call this function.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateFileEx(PHANDLE FileHandle, ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock, PLARGE_INTEGER AllocationSize, ULONG FileAttributes, ULONG ShareAccess, ULONG Disposition, ULONG CreateOptions, PVOID EaBuffer, ULONG EaLength, CREATE_FILE_TYPE CreateFileType, PVOID InternalParameters, ULONG Options, PIO_DRIVER_CREATE_CONTEXT DriverContext);

params.name: FileHandle
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the file handle if the call is successful. The driver must close the handle with ZwClose as soon as the handle is no longer being used.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: A bitmask of flags (see ACCESS_MASK) that specifies the type of access that the caller requires to the file or directory. This set of system-defined *DesiredAccess* flags determines the following specific access rights for file objects.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: Pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure already initialized by the InitializeObjectAttributes function. If the caller is running in the system process context, this parameter can be NULL. Otherwise, the caller must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute in the call to InitializeObjectAttributes. Members of this structure for a file object include the following.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: Pointer to a variable of type IO_STATUS_BLOCK that receives the final completion status and information about the requested operation. On return from IoCreateFileEx, the Information member of the variable contains one of the following values:

params.name: AllocationSize
params.description: Optionally specifies the initial allocation size, in bytes, for the file. A nonzero value has no effect unless the file is being created, overwritten, or superseded.

params.name: FileAttributes
params.description: Explicitly specified attributes are applied only when the file is created, superseded, or, in some cases, overwritten. By default, this value is FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, which can be overridden by any other flag or by a combination (through a bitwise OR operation) of compatible flags. Possible *FileAttributes* flags include the following.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the type of share access to the file that the caller would like, as zero, or one, or a combination of the following flags. To request exclusive access, set this parameter to zero. If the IO_IGNORE_SHARE_ACCESS_CHECK flag is specified in the *Options* parameter, the I/O manager ignores the *ShareAccess* parameter. However, the file system might still perform access checks. Thus, it is important to specify the sharing mode you would like for this parameter, even when you use the IO_IGNORE_SHARE_ACCESS_CHECK flag. To help you avoid sharing violation errors, specify all the following share access flags.

params.name: Disposition
params.description: Value that determines how the file should be handled when the file already exists. *Disposition* can be one of the following.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Specifies the options to be applied when creating or opening the file, as a compatible combination of the following flags.

params.name: EaBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied variable of type FILE_FULL_EA_INFORMATION that contains extended attribute (EA) information to be applied to the file. For device and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be NULL.

params.name: EaLength
params.description: Length, in bytes, of *EaBuffer*. For device drivers and intermediate drivers, this parameter must be zero.

params.name: CreateFileType
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to CreateFileTypeNone.

params.name: InternalParameters
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to NULL.

params.name: Options
params.description: Specifies options to be used during the generation of the create request. Zero or more of the following bit flag values can be used.

params.name: DriverContext
params.description: An optional pointer to an IO_DRIVER_CREATE_CONTEXT structure that was previously initialized by the IoInitializeDriverCreateContext function. The IO_DRIVER_CREATE_CONTEXT structure can be used to pass additional parameters to the IoCreateFileEx and FltCreateFileEx2 functions. See the following Remarks section for more information.

returns.description: IoCreateFileEx either returns STATUS_SUCCESS or an appropriate NTSTATUS value such as one of the following.

functions.name: IoCreateFileSpecifyDeviceObjectHint
functions.summary: The IoCreateFileSpecifyDeviceObjectHint function is used by file system filter drivers to send a create request only to the filters below a specified device object and to the file system.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoCreateFileSpecifyDeviceObjectHint(PHANDLE FileHandle, ACCESS_MASK DesiredAccess, POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES ObjectAttributes, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock, PLARGE_INTEGER AllocationSize, ULONG FileAttributes, ULONG ShareAccess, ULONG Disposition, ULONG CreateOptions, PVOID EaBuffer, ULONG EaLength, CREATE_FILE_TYPE CreateFileType, PVOID InternalParameters, ULONG Options, PVOID DeviceObject);

params.name: FileHandle
params.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a handle for the file object if this call is successful.

params.name: DesiredAccess
params.description: A bitmask of flags that specify the type of access that the caller requires to the file or directory. The set of system-defined *DesiredAccess* flags determines the following specific access rights for file objects.

params.name: ObjectAttributes
params.description: A pointer to an OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure already initialized by the InitializeObjectAttributes function. If the caller is running in the system process context, this parameter (*ObjectAttributes*) can be NULL. Otherwise, the caller must set the OBJ_KERNEL_HANDLE attribute in the call to the InitializeObjectAttributes function. Members of the OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES structure for a file object include the following.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: A pointer to an IO_STATUS_BLOCK structure that receives the final completion status and information about the requested operation. On return from IoCreateFileSpecifyDeviceObjectHint, the Information member contains one of the following values:

params.name: AllocationSize
params.description: Optionally specifies the initial allocation size, in bytes, for the file. A nonzero value has no effect unless the file is being created, overwritten, or superseded.

params.name: FileAttributes
params.description: Explicitly specified attributes are applied only when the file is created, superseded, or, in some cases, overwritten. By default, this value is FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, which can be overridden by any other flag or by an ORed combination of compatible flags. Possible *FileAttributes* flags include the following.

params.name: ShareAccess
params.description: Specifies the type of share access to the file that the caller would like, as zero, or one, or a combination of the following flags. To request exclusive access, set this parameter to zero. If the IO_IGNORE_SHARE_ACCESS_CHECK flag is specified in the *Options* parameter, the I/O manager ignores this parameter. However, the file system might still perform access checks. Thus, it is important to specify the sharing mode you would like for this parameter, even when using the IO_IGNORE_SHARE_ACCESS_CHECK flag. For the greatest chance of avoiding sharing violation errors, specify all of the following share access flags.

params.name: Disposition
params.description: Specifies a value that determines the action to be taken, depending on whether the file already exists. The value can be any of those described following.

params.name: CreateOptions
params.description: Specifies the options to be applied when creating or opening the file. These options are specified as a compatible combination of the following flags.

params.name: EaBuffer
params.description: A pointer to a caller-supplied FILE_FULL_EA_INFORMATION-structured buffer containing extended attribute (EA) information to be applied to the file.

params.name: EaLength
params.description: The length, in bytes, of *EaBuffer*.

params.name: CreateFileType
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to CreateFileTypeNone.

params.name: InternalParameters
params.description: Drivers must set this parameter to NULL.

params.name: Options
params.description: Specifies options to be used during the creation of the create request. The following table lists the available options.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to the device object to which the create request is to be sent. The device object must be a filter or file system device object in the file system driver stack for the volume on which the file or directory resides. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. params.name: Irp
params.description: Pointer to the IRP that failed because of a device I/O error.

params.name: Vpb

params.name: RealDeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object that represents the physical device on which the I/O operation failed.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoRaiseInformationalHardError
functions.summary: The IoRaiseInformationalHardError function sends a dialog box to the user, warning about a device I/O error that indicates why a user I/O request failed.
functions.signature: BOOLEAN IoRaiseInformationalHardError(NTSTATUS ErrorStatus, PUNICODE_STRING String, PKTHREAD Thread);

params.name: ErrorStatus
params.description: The error status code (IO_ERR_XXX).

params.name: String
params.description: A pointer to a Unicode string, which provides additional information about the error. Some NT status codes require a string parameter, such as a file or directory name. If the specified ErrorStatus value does not require a string parameter, set String to NULL.

params.name: Thread
params.description: A pointer to the thread whose IRP was failed due to the error specified by the ErrorStatus parameter.

returns.description: IoRaiseInformationalHardError returns TRUE if the dialog box was successfully queued. This function returns FALSE if dialog boxes are disabled for Thread, a pool allocation failed, too many dialog boxes are already queued, or an equivalent dialog box is already pending a user response (such as waiting for the user to press RETURN).

functions.name: IoReadDiskSignature
functions.summary: The IoReadDiskSignature function reads the disk signature information for the partition table of a disk.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoReadDiskSignature(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, ULONG BytesPerSector, PDISK_SIGNATURE Signature);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Specifies the device object for the disk to read.

params.name: BytesPerSector
params.description: Specifies the number of bytes per sector of the disk.

params.name: Signature
params.description: Pointer to a DISK_SIGNATURE structure the function uses to return the disk signature information.

returns.description: The function returns STATUS_SUCCESS on success, or the appropriate error code on failure. The function returns STATUS_DISK_CORRUPT_ERROR if it detects that the disk partition table is corrupted.

functions.name: IoReadPartitionTable
functions.summary: The IoReadPartitionTable function is obsolete and is provided only to support existing drivers. New drivers must use IoReadPartitionTableEx. IoReadPartitionTable reads a list of partitions on a disk having a specified sector size and creates an entry in the partition list for each recognized partition.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoReadPartitionTable(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, ULONG SectorSize, BOOLEAN ReturnRecognizedPartitions, struct _DRIVE_LAYOUT_INFORMATION ** PartitionBuffer);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object for the disk whose partitions are to be read.

params.name: SectorSize
params.description: Specifies the size of the sectors on the disk.

params.name: ReturnRecognizedPartitions
params.description: Indicates whether only recognized partitions or all partition entries should be returned.

params.name: PartitionBuffer
params.description: Pointer to an uninitialized address. If successful, IoReadPartitionTable allocates the memory for this buffer from nonpaged pool and returns the drive layout information in it.

returns.description: This function returns a value of STATUS_SUCCESS if at least one sector table was read. Otherwise, it returns an error status and sets the pointer at PartitionBuffer to NULL.

functions.name: IoReadPartitionTableEx
functions.summary: The IoReadPartitionTableEx function reads a list of partitions on a disk having a specified sector size and creates an entry in the partition list for each recognized partition.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object for the disk whose partitions are to be read.

params.name: DriveLayout
params.description: Pointer to an uninitialized address. If successful, IoReadPartitionTableEx allocates the memory for this buffer from nonpaged pool and returns the drive layout information in it.

returns.description: This function returns a value of STATUS_SUCCESS if at least one sector table was read. Otherwise, it returns an error status value and sets the pointer at PartitionBuffer to NULL.

functions.name: IoRegisterBootDriverCallback
functions.summary: The IoRegisterBootDriverCallback function registers a BOOT_DRIVER_CALLBACK_FUNCTION function to be called during the initialization of a boot-start driver and its dependent DLLs.

params.name: CallbackFunction
params.description: A pointer to the BOOT_DRIVER_CALLBACK_FUNCTION function to be called when initializing a boot-start driver or DLL.

params.name: CallbackContext
params.description: A driver-defined context to be passed to the BOOT_DRIVER_CALLBACK_FUNCTION function pointed to by CallbackFunction.

functions.name: IoRegisterBootDriverReinitialization

params.name: DriverObject

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoRegisterDriverReinitialization
functions.summary: The IoRegisterDriverReinitialization function is called by a driver during its initialization or reinitialization to register its Reinitialize function to be called again before the driver's and, possibly the system's, initialization is complete.
functions.signature: void IoRegisterDriverReinitialization(PDRIVER_OBJECT DriverObject, PDRIVER_REINITIALIZE DriverReinitializationRoutine, PVOID Context);

params.name: DriverObject

params.name: DriverReinitializationRoutine
params.description: Pointer to the driver's Reinitialize function.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoReportDetectedDevice
functions.summary: The IoReportDetectedDevice function reports a non-PnP device to the PnP manager.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoReportDetectedDevice(PDRIVER_OBJECT DriverObject, INTERFACE_TYPE LegacyBusType, ULONG BusNumber, ULONG SlotNumber, PCM_RESOURCE_LIST ResourceList, PIO_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_LIST ResourceRequirements, BOOLEAN ResourceAssigned, PDEVICE_OBJECT * DeviceObject);

params.name: DriverObject
params.description: Pointer to the driver object of the driver that detected the device.

params.name: LegacyBusType
params.description: Specifies the type of bus on which the device resides. The PnP manager uses this information to match the reported device to its PnP-enumerated instance, if one exists.

params.name: BusNumber
params.description: Specifies the bus number for the device. The PnP manager uses this information to match the reported device to its PnP-enumerated instance, if one exists.

params.name: SlotNumber
params.description: Specifies the logical slot number of the device. The PnP manager uses this information to match the reported device to its PnP-enumerated instance, if one exists.

params.name: ResourceList
params.description: Pointer to the resource list the driver used to detect the device. Resources in this list are in raw, untranslated form.

params.name: ResourceRequirements
params.description: Optionally points to a resource requirements list for the detected device. NULL if the caller does not have this information for the device.

params.name: ResourceAssigned
params.description: Specifies whether the device's resources have already been reported to the PnP manager. If ResourceAssigned is TRUE, the resources have already been reported, possibly with IoReportResourceForDetection, and the PnP manager will not attempt to claim them on behalf of the device. If TRUE, the PnP manager will also not claim resources when the device is root-enumerated on subsequent boots.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Optionally points to a PDO for the detected device.

returns.description: IoReportDetectedDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS on success, or the appropriate error code on failure.

functions.name: IoReportResourceForDetection
functions.summary: The IoReportResourceForDetection function claims hardware resources in the configuration registry for a legacy device.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoReportResourceForDetection(PDRIVER_OBJECT DriverObject, PCM_RESOURCE_LIST DriverList, ULONG DriverListSize, PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, PCM_RESOURCE_LIST DeviceList, ULONG DeviceListSize, PBOOLEAN ConflictDetected);

params.name: DriverObject
params.description: Pointer to the driver object that was input to the driver's DriverEntry function.

params.name: DriverList
params.description: Optionally points to a caller-supplied buffer that contains the driver's resource list, if the driver claims the same resources for all its devices. If the caller specifies a *DeviceList*, this parameter is ignored.

params.name: DriverListSize
params.description: Specifies the size in bytes of an optional *DriverList*. If *DriverList* is NULL, this parameter should be zero.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Optionally points to the device object representing device for which the driver is attempting to claim resources.

params.name: DeviceList
params.description: Optionally points to a caller-supplied buffer containing the device's resource list. If the driver claims the same resources for all its devices, the caller can specify a *DriverList* instead.

params.name: DeviceListSize
params.description: Specifies the size in bytes of an optional *DeviceList*. If *DeviceList* is NULL, this parameter should be zero.

params.name: ConflictDetected
params.description: Pointer to a caller-supplied Boolean value that is set to TRUE on return if the resources are not available.

returns.description: IoReportResourceForDetection returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the resources are claimed. Possible error return values include the following.

functions.name: IoReportRootDevice
functions.summary: The IoReportRootDevice function reports a device that cannot be detected by a PnP bus driver to the PnP Manager. IoReportRootDevice allows only one device per driver to be created.

params.name: DriverObject
params.description: Pointer to the driver object of the driver that detected the device.

returns.description: IoReportRootDevice returns STATUS_SUCCESS on success, or the appropriate error code on failure.

params.description: The IRP to associate the activity ID with.

params.name: Guid
params.description: A pointer to the GUID that represents the ID to store in the IRP. If NULL, IoSetActivityIdIrp attempts to retrieve the activity ID from the current thread if it was the thread that originally issued the request.

params.name: ActivityId

returns.description: The activity ID that was previously set on the thread. Drivers must call IoClearActivityIdThread with this pointer when tracing is completed within the same thread context.

functions.name: IoSetFileObjectIgnoreSharing
functions.summary: The IoSetFileObjectIgnoreSharing function sets a file object to ignore file sharing access checks.

params.name: FileObject
params.description: Pointer to a file object for the file.

functions.name: IoSetHardErrorOrVerifyDevice
functions.summary: Lower-level drivers call the IoSetHardErrorOrVerifyDevice function to identify a removable media device that has encountered an error, so that a file system driver can prompt the user to verify that the medium is valid.

params.name: Irp

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the target device to be verified for the I/O operation.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoSetMasterIrpStatus
functions.summary: The IoSetMasterIrpStatus function conditionally replaces the Status value in an IRP with the specified NTSTATUS value.

params.name: MasterIrp
params.description: A pointer to the master IRP. For more information, see Remarks.

params.name: Status
params.description: An NTSTATUS value to compare to the Status member of the I/O status block in the master IRP.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoSetPartitionInformation
functions.summary: The IoSetPartitionInformation function is obsolete and is provided only to support existing drivers. New drivers must use IoSetPartitionInformationEx.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoSetPartitionInformation(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, ULONG SectorSize, ULONG PartitionNumber, ULONG PartitionType);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object representing the device on which the partition type is to be set.

params.name: SectorSize

params.name: PartitionNumber
params.description: Specifies the partition number on the device whose partition type is to be set.

params.name: PartitionType
params.description: Specifies the type for the partition. For a list of some of the key partition types see PARTITION_INFORMATION.

returns.description: If IoSetPartitionInformation returns STATUS_SUCCESS, the disk driver updates its notion of the partition type for this partition in its device extension.

functions.name: IoSetPartitionInformationEx
functions.summary: For the disk represented by DeviceObject, the IoSetPartitionInformationEx function initializes a partition table entry with the information specified in the SET_PARTITION_INFORMATION_EX structure.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS IoSetPartitionInformationEx(PDEVICE_OBJECT DeviceObject, ULONG PartitionNumber, struct _SET_PARTITION_INFORMATION_EX * PartitionInfo);

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Pointer to the device object representing the device on which the partition type is to be set.

params.name: PartitionNumber
params.description: Specifies the partition number on the device whose partition type is to be set.

params.name: PartitionInfo
params.description: A structure whose PartitionType member specifies the type for the partition. For the currently defined PartitionType values PARTITION_INFORMATION.

returns.description: If IoSetPartitionInformationEx returns STATUS_SUCCESS, the disk driver updates its notion of the partition type for this partition in its device extension.

functions.name: IoSetShadowFileInformation
functions.summary: This topic describes the IoSetShadowFileInformation function.

params.name: FileObject

params.name: BackingFileObject
params.description: Defines the PFILE_OBJECT parameter *BackingFileObject*.

returns.description: NTSTATUS

functions.name: IoSetSystemPartition
functions.summary: The IoSetSystemPartition function sets the boot partition for the system.

params.name: VolumeNameString
params.description: Pointer to a Unicode string that specifies the MS-DOS name of the system partition.

returns.description: STATUS_SUCCESS if the boot partition can be set, or an error code on failure.

functions.name: IoSetThreadHardErrorMode
functions.summary: The IoSetThreadHardErrorMode function enables or disables hard error reporting for the current thread.

params.name: EnableHardErrors
params.description: Specifies whether hard error reporting to the user should be enabled or disabled for this thread. A value of TRUE enables hard error reporting. FALSE disables it.

returns.description: IoSetThreadHardErrorMode returns TRUE if hard errors were enabled from this thread before this function completed execution. Otherwise, this function returns FALSE.

functions.name: IoTransferActivityId
functions.summary: The IoTransferActivityId function logs an ETW transfer event using the I/O tracing provider on behalf of the caller. This allows a driver to associate two related activity IDs without requiring a specific provider to be enabled.

params.name: ActivityId

params.name: RelatedActivityId

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoUnregisterBootDriverCallback
functions.summary: The IoUnRegisterBootDriverCallback function unregisters a previously registered BOOT_DRIVER_CALLBACK_FUNCTION function.

params.name: CallbackHandle
params.description: A handle returned from a previous call to IoRegisterBootDriverCallback.

returns.description: No value.

functions.name: IoVerifyPartitionTable
functions.summary: The IoVerifyPartitionTable function checks the validity of the partition table for a disk.

params.name: DeviceObject
params.description: Specifies the device object of the disk to verify.

params.name: FixErrors
params.description: Specifies if the function should correct any correctable errors in the partition table.

returns.description: The function returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the partition table is error-free.

functions.name: IoVolumeDeviceToDosName
functions.summary: The IoVolumeDeviceToDosName function returns the MS-DOS path for a specified device object that represents a file system volume.

params.name: VolumeDeviceObject
params.description: A pointer to a device object that represents a volume device object created by a storage class driver.

params.description: A pointer to a caller-allocated UNICODE_STRING structure. If the call is successful, IoVolumeDeviceToDosName sets the values of the Length, MaximumLength, and Buffer members of this structure. returns.description: IoVolumeDeviceToDosName returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the call is successful. Possible error return values include the following status codes.

params.name: PartitionBuffer

functions.name: KeExpandKernelStackAndCallout

params.name: Callout
params.description: Pointer to an ExpandedStackCall function.

functions.name: KeExpandKernelStackAndCalloutEx
functions.summary: The KeExpandKernelStackAndCalloutEx function calls a function and guarantees that a specified amount of stack space is available for this call.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS KeExpandKernelStackAndCalloutEx(PEXPAND_STACK_CALLOUT Callout, PVOID Parameter, SIZE_T Size, BOOLEAN Wait, PVOID Context);

params.name: Callout
params.description: A function pointer to an *ExpandedStackCall* function. KeExpandKernelStackAndCalloutEx expands the stack, if necessary, before it calls this function.

params.name: Parameter

functions.name: MmCopyMemory

functions.summary: The MmSecureVirtualMemory function secures a user-space memory address range so that it cannot be freed and its page protection cannot be made more restrictive.

functions.name: ZwDeviceIoControlFile
functions.summary: The ZwDeviceIoControlFile function sends a control code directly to a specified device driver, causing the corresponding driver to perform the specified operation.
functions.signature: NTSTATUS ZwDeviceIoControlFile(HANDLE FileHandle, HANDLE Event, PIO_APC_ROUTINE ApcRoutine, PVOID ApcContext, PIO_STATUS_BLOCK IoStatusBlock, ULONG IoControlCode, PVOID InputBuffer, ULONG InputBufferLength, PVOID OutputBuffer, ULONG OutputBufferLength);

params.name: FileHandle
params.description: Handle returned by ZwCreateFile or ZwOpenFile for the file object representing the device to which the control information should be given or from which information should be returned. The file object must have been opened for asynchronous I/O if the caller specifies an *Event*, *ApcRoutine*, and an APC context (in *ApcContext*), or a completion context (in *ApcContext*). For I/O to an underlying mass-storage device, the file object must have been opened for Direct Access to Storage Device (DASD) access.

params.name: Event
params.description: Handle for a caller-created event. If this parameter is supplied, the caller will be put into a wait state until the requested operation is completed and the given event is set to the Signaled state. This parameter is optional and can be NULL. It must be NULL if the caller will wait for the *FileHandle* to be set to the Signaled state.

params.name: ApcRoutine
params.description: Address of an optional, caller-supplied APC function to be called when the requested operation completes. This parameter can be NULL. It must be NULL if there is an I/O completion object associated with the file object.

params.name: ApcContext
params.description: Pointer to a caller-determined context area. This parameter value is used as the APC context if the caller supplies an APC, or is used as the completion context if an I/O completion object has been associated with the file object. When the operation completes, either the APC context is passed to the APC, if one was specified, or the completion context is included as part of the completion message that the I/O Manager posts to the associated I/O completion object.

params.name: IoStatusBlock
params.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the final completion status and information about the operation. For successful calls that return data, the number of bytes written to the *OutputBuffer* is returned in the Information member.

params.name: IoControlCode
params.description: IOCTL_*XXX* code that indicates which device I/O control operation is to be carried out on, usually by the underlying device driver. The value of this parameter determines the format and required length of the *InputBuffer* and *OutputBuffer*, as well as which of the following parameter pairs are required. For detailed information about the system-defined, device-type-specific IOCTL_*XXX* codes, see the device technology-specific section of the Microsoft Windows Driver Kit (WDK) documentation and Device Input and Output Control Codes in the Microsoft Windows SDK documentation.

params.name: InputBuffer
params.description: Pointer to a caller-allocated input buffer that contains device-specific information to be given to the target device. If *IoControlCode* specifies an operation that does not require input data, this pointer can be NULL.

params.name: InputBufferLength
params.description: Size, in bytes, of the buffer at *InputBuffer*. If *InputBuffer* is NULL, set *InputBufferLength* to zero.

params.name: OutputBuffer
params.description: Pointer to a caller-allocated output buffer in which information is returned from the target device. If *IoControlCode* specifies an operation that does not produce output data, this pointer can be NULL.

params.name: OutputBufferLength
params.description: Size, in bytes, of the buffer at *OutputBuffer*. If *OutputBuffer* is NULL, set *OutputBufferLength* to zero.
